title: How Leaders Help to Create Brilliant Jerks
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece confronts the uncomfortable dynamic of high-performing but toxic team members, sometimes called Brilliant Jerks, and argues that leaders themselves usually help create them. Because these individuals are richly rewarded for results while their behavior is tolerated, the culture teaches them that how they get there matters far less than whether they deliver. Rather than defaulting to termination, which the author calls impractical and only partly fair given the leader's own role in the pattern, the piece recommends resetting expectations so that both results and respectful behavior are explicitly required and rewarded. That means team members holding firm to new standards and compensation structures actually following through, with leader-driven accountability underpinning the whole reset.
points: Brilliant Jerks are high performers who behave in disruptive or toxic ways and are still tolerated.
Leaders and teams typically co-create this dynamic by rewarding results while excusing bad behavior.
Simply firing the top performer is often impractical and only partly addresses the real problem.
The better fix is resetting expectations so results and respectful behavior are both required and rewarded.
quotes: These are team members who achieve great results but consistently display disruptive, inconsiderate, or toxic behavior.
The real quandary is for the leader and the team to recognize and admit that they have had a heavy hand in producing them.
High-performing Skunks behave badly because they can, and they are typically highly rewarded for it.
The better course of action is to reset expectations and to impress upon the Brilliant Jerk that both results and respectful behavior are equally important.
Leaders get what they implicitly endorse and tolerate. So, who is the real jerk?
